headline: Every element of PGL_2(F_q), for every prime power q, has exactly one of four projective-line cycle types; fixed, primitive, zeta, reversor, and finite Koopman data close exactly.
nonclaims: literature priority for the classical conjugacy classification
that the finite test set proves the arbitrary-prime-power theorem
a rational-prime primitive-orbit dictionary or logarithmic prime clock
target arithmetic local data, Euler factors, root numbers, automorphy, divisor, or functional equation
a target Fredholm determinant, Hilbert--Polya operator, or Route-B authorization

route_a.strongest_failure: no rational-prime primitive carrier, log-prime clock, target divisor, target analytic continuation, or Hilbert--Polya identification
route_a.strongest_positive: all-prime-power analytic cycle classification and a canonical finite same-clock unitary Koopman owner

theorem.characteristic_two: tr(A)=0 gives the repeated-root face; otherwise Tr_Fq/F2(det(A)/tr(A)^2) distinguishes split zero from nonsplit one
theorem.classification: identity, nontrivial unipotent, split semisimple, or nonsplit semisimple
theorem.fixed: #Fix(g^n) is the sum of cycle lengths dividing n
theorem.koopman: det(I-t U_g)=zeta_g(t)^(-1); each L-cycle contributes every L-th root once
theorem.nonsplit: eigenvalue-ratio order d|q+1 and cycle type d^((q+1)/d)
theorem.reversor: in a cyclic basis H=[[0,det(A)],[1,0]] is projectively involutive and conjugates g to g^(-1)
theorem.route_boundary: finite-field arithmetic supplies no rational-prime orbit dictionary, logarithmic prime clock, target divisor, or Hilbert--Polya identification
theorem.split: eigenvalue-ratio order d|q-1 and cycle type 1^2 d^((q-1)/d)
theorem.type_census: unipotent q^2-1; split order d count q(q+1)phi(d)/2; nonsplit order d count q(q-1)phi(d)/2
theorem.unipotent: order p and cycle type 1^1 p^(q/p)
